Nice!  Question:  There is lots of software already doing things like `.gsub("fcr:versions", "fcr%3Aversions")` as a workaround. Since this problem has existed for at least two and a half years, the workaround has become embedded in lots of client code. Will the fix break this code, being effectively a backwards compat problem? That is, will the "fcr%3Aversions" version of the URI still be resolvable?  Is there any way to maybe make a switch or something to at least temporarily make it so, to avoid breaking all the software that has been working around the problem for a couple years?
URL Encoding the colon in fcr:versions effectively does the same thing as my change, it causes the Jersey Path matcher to

match and so it passes through to the fcr:fixity which does match. This means that this change _should_ have no effect on your workflow, other than you no longer need to URL encode the fcr:versions in the URL.
I'd (of course) suggest you give it a test to make sure, but as this is a single line change and does not affect how either versions or fixity operates I think the impact should be negligible.
This task is to determine why "fcr%3aversions" is not being decoded and interpreted in the example detailed here:
Then, likely update the logic to decode the URL but recognize the "fcr" prefix and treat it differently.
The issue is that we map URLs based on their structure and in Jersey if you have a URL
Then Jersey acts on the path match closest to the hostname first (action1 in my example), then the next one (action2) and so on (action3).

So in our case we are matching on fcr:versions first and trying to perform this action. FedoraVersions doesn't handle fcr:fixity (nor expects it to be in the URL) so it fails. My assumption is that if this had succeeded then Fedora would have attempted to perform the fcr:fixity tasks next.
My solution was to alter the fcr:versions @Path matching to
match if the URL has fcr:versions but ends with fcr:fixity.

comments.body: Since supporting fixity checks on historic versions is a feature we support we should ensure that there's an integration test in our code base. This ticket might be a good opportunity to sure that up.

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/fedora-tech/qw3GlptWBQw/Pmly99yHoDIJ says:

the odd part is why the URL encoding is not being decoded in the path interpretation. But under the circumstances, it is a good thing. The logic should probably be to decode the URL but recognize the "fcr" prefix and treat it differently.

I'm not sure it is clear what the desired behavior should be. I presume it's about interpreting localhost:8080/rest/collection/image/fcr:versions/v0/fcr:fixity as a fcr:fixity directive without having to encode fcr:versions into fcr%3Aversions to prevent it from being taken for a directive?

fcrepo is actually delivering URLs that can't be resolved.  If you look at the HTML version (or a triple version) of a page with fixity, it will contain URLs like "localhost:8080/rest/collection/image/fcr:versions/v0/fcr:fixity", that, if you click on them, give you an error. You have to yourself modify the URL to change "fcr:versions" to "fcr%3Aversions". 

Surely this is a bug one way or the other, whichever is the 'correct' URI, the URI returned in a response ought to be resolvable without external transformation. 

It makes it much more difficult to deal with the platform that I can't take a URI returned by it and assume it's resolvable – I need to apply some not entirely specified transformations to it to make it resolvable. ("fcr:versions" whenever it appears? Or sometimes not?  Any other strings? Etc.).

I have confirmed this behaviour and it seems to be because based on the Jersey @Path parameter, the fcr:versions is handled before the fcr:fixity.

Andrew Woods suggested URL-encoding the fcr:versions in the Link Header (ie. Link <http://localhost:8080/rest/this_thing/fcr%3Aversions/v0/fcr:fixity;rel="hasFixityService">), which would work because Jersey would no longer match the fcr:versions path, but does seem odd compared to the other Link headers.

Also the error will still occur, just that we have changed the URI for the versions fixity service.

The only other alternative I can think of is to modify FedoraVersions to not match if the Request URI ends with fcr:fixity and allow it to fall through to FedoraFixity.

I'm experimenting with the Jersey @Path parameter, if anyone has a suggestion I'll take it.

I'm only peripherally following this, but I gather this is not exactly a URL decoding issue - Jared Whiklo would you mind updating the description on this ticket to something more relevant to the identified problem and solution for future us?

Andrew Woods Nice!  Question:  There is lots of software already doing things like `.gsub("fcr:versions", "fcr%3Aversions")` as a workaround. Since this problem has existed for at least two and a half years, the workaround has become embedded in lots of client code. Will the fix break this code, being effectively a backwards compat problem? That is, will the "fcr%3Aversions" version of the URI still be resolvable?  Is there any way to maybe make a switch or something to at least temporarily make it so, to avoid breaking all the software that has been working around the problem for a couple years?

jrochkind URL Encoding the colon in fcr:versions effectively does the same thing as my change, it causes the Jersey Path matcher to not match and so it passes through to the fcr:fixity which does match. This means that this change should have no effect on your workflow, other than you no longer need to URL encode the fcr:versions in the URL.

I'd (of course) suggest you give it a test to make sure, but as this is a single line change and does not affect how either versions or fixity operates I think the impact should be negligible.

Then, likely update the logic to decode the URL but recognize the "fcr" prefix and treat it differently.

*Background of issue (by Jared)*
The issue is that we map URLs based on their structure and in Jersey if you have a URL
http://localhost:8080/base/action1/action2/action3
and mappings
Path = .*/action1
Path = .*/action2
Path = .*/action3

Then Jersey acts on the path match closest to the hostname first (action1 in my example), then the next one (action2) and so on (action3).

So in our case we are matching on fcr:versions first and trying to perform this action. FedoraVersions doesn't handle fcr:fixity (nor expects it to be in the URL) so it fails. My assumption is that if this had succeeded then Fedora would have attempted to perform the fcr:fixity tasks next.

My solution was to alter the fcr:versions @Path matching to not match if the URL has fcr:versions but ends with fcr:fixity.
